UNDERSET: To prop or support. Bacon. Undercurrent.
UNVISARD: To take the vizard or mask from; to unmask. [Written also unvizard.] [Obs.] Milton.

UNCORRUPTIBLE: Incorruptible. "The glory of the uncorruptible God." Rom. i. 23.

ULNAR: Of or pertaining to the ulna, or the elbow; as, the ulnar nerve.
UNDERTENANT: The tenant of a tenant; one who holds lands or tenements of a tenant or lessee.

UNGIVE: To yield; to relax; to give way. [Obs.]
UNWARM: To lose warmth; to grow cold. [R.]
UNEXPERIENCED: 1. Not experienced; being without experience; inexperienced. Swift. 2. Untried; -- applied to things. Cheyne.

UNTREAD: To tread back; to retrace. Shak.

ULTRAZODIACAL: Outside the zodiac; being in that part of the heavens that is more than eight degrees from the ecliptic; as, ultrazodiacal planets, that is, those planets which in part of their orbits go beyond the zodiac.
UNIFIER: One who, or that which, unifies; as, a natural law is a unifier of phenomena.
UNCLINCH: To cause to be no longer clinched; to open; as, to unclinch the fist. [Written also unclench.]
URANOPLASTY: The plastic operation for closing a fissure in the hard palate.
UNREMEMBRANCE: Want of remembrance; forgetfulness. I. Watts.
UNPRICED: Not priced; being without a fixed or certain value; also, priceless. "Amethyst unpriced." Neale (Rhythm of St. Bernard).
UNPACK: 1. To separate and remove, as things packed; to open and remove the contents of; as, to unpack a trunk. 2. To relieve of a pack or burden. [R.] Shak.
UNDERLING: An inferior person or agent; a subordinate; hence, a mean, sorry fellow. Milton. he fault, dear Brutus, is not in our stars, But in ourselves, that we are underlings. Shak.
UNADULTERATE: Not adulterated; pure. "Unadulterate air." Cowper. -- Un`a*dul"ter*ate*ly, adv.
UNBEGOT: Not begot; not yet generated; also, having never been generated; self-existent; eternal.
UNICENTRAL: Having a single center of growth. Unicentral development, that form of development which takes place primarily around a single central point, as in the lowest of unicellular organisms.
UT: The first note in Guido's musical scale, now usually superseded by do. See Solmization.
UPSTAIRS: Up the stairs; in or toward an upper story. Being above stairs; as, an upstairs room.
UNMOOR: (a) To cause to ride with one anchor less than before, after having been moored by two or more anchors. (b) To loose from anchorage. See Moor, v. t. To weigh anchor. Sir W. Scott.
UNA BOAT: The English name for a catboat; -- so called because Una was the name of the first boat of this kind taken to England. D. Kemp.
UNFILIAL: Unsuitable to a son or a daughter; undutiful; not becoming a child. -- Un*fil"ial*ly, adv.
UNCLEW: To unwind, unfold, or untie; hence, to undo; to ruin. Shak.
UNCLOTHE: To strip of clothes or covering; to make naked. I. Watts. [We] do groan being burdened; not for that we would be unclothed, but clothed upon. 2 Cor. v. 4.
UNCONTINENT: Not continent; incontinent. Wyclif (2 Tim. iii. 3).
UNDERWORKER: 1. One who underworks. 2. An inferior or subordinate workman. Waterland.
UNBEHOVELY: Not behooving or becoming; unseemly. [Obs. & R.] Gower.
UNDISPENSED: 1. Not dispensed. 2. Not freed by dispensation. [R.] Tooker.
UNHALLOW: To profane; to desecrate. The vanity unhallows the virtue. L'Estrange.
UNHAT: To take off the hat of; to remove one's hat, especially as a mark of respect. H. Spenser.
UNDERCHAMBERLAIN: A deputy chamberlain of the exchequer.
UNANIMITY: The quality or state of being unanimous.
UNBRACE: To free from tension; to relax; to loose; as, to unbrace a drum; to unbrace the nerves. Spenser.
UNVALUED: 1. Not valued; not appraised; hence, not considered; disregarded; valueless; as, an unvalued estate. "Unvalued persons." Shak. 2. Having inestimable value; invaluable. [Obs.] The golden apples of unvalued price. Spenser.
UNTACK: To separate, as what is tacked; to disjoin; to release. being untacked from honest cares. Barrow.
UNIFY: To cause to be one; to make into a unit; to unite; to view as one. A comprehensive or unifying act of the judging faculty. De Quincey. Perception is thus a unifying act. Sir W. Hamilton.
UNFAILING: Not failing; not liable to fail; inexhaustible; certain; sure. Dryden. -- Un*fail"ing*ly, adv. -- Un*fail"ing*ness, n.
UNFENCE: To strip of a fence; to remove a fence from.
UNRESTRAINT: Freedom from restraint; freedom; liberty; license.
UNHOARD: To take or steal from a hoard; to pilfer. Milton.
UNGOWNED: 1. Etym: [1 st pref. un- + gown.] Stripped of a gown; unfrocked. 2. Etym: [Pref. un- not + gowned.] Not having, or not wearing, a gown.
UNMERCIFUL: Not merciful; indisposed to mercy or grace; cruel; inhuman; merciless; unkind. -- Un*mer"ci*ful*ly, adv. -- Un*mer"ci*ful*ness, n.
UNPRINCE: To deprive of the character or authority of a prince; to divest of principality of sovereignty. [R.] Swift.
UNBEGUN: Not yet begun; also, existing without a beginning.
UNDETERMINATE: Nor determinate; not settled or certain; indeterminate. South. -- Un`de*ter"mi*nate*ness, n. Dr. H. More.
UNLINE: To take the lining out of; hence, to empty; as, to unline one's purse.
UNIBRANCHIATE: Having but one gill, as certain molluscs.
UNIMPROVED: 1. Not improved; not made better or wiser; not advanced in knowledge, manners, or excellence. 2. Not used; not employed; especially, not used or employed for a valuable purpose; as, unimproved opportunities; unimproved blessings. Cowper. 3. Not tilled, cultivated, or built upon; yielding no revenue; as, unimproved land or soil.
UNDERLET: 1. To let below the value. All my farms were underlet. Smollett. 2. To let or lease at second hand; to sublet.
UNPROMISE: To revoke or annul, as a promise. Chapman.
UNMOVED: Not moved; fixed; firm; unshaken; calm; apathetic. -- Un*mov"ed*ly, adv.
UNKINDRED: Not kindred; not of the same kin. [Obs.] Rowe. -- Un*kin"dred*ly, a.
UNFRIENDED: Wanting friends; not befriended; not countenanced or supported. Goldsmith. If Richard indeed does come back, it must be alone, unfollowed, unfriended. Sir W. Scott.
UNSEEMLY: Not seemly; unbecoming; indecent. An unseemly outbreak of temper. Hawthorne. In an unseemly manner.
UNQUALITIED: Deprived of the usual faculties. [Obs.] Shak.
UNWEIGHED: Not weighed; not pondered or considered; as, an unweighed statement.
UNCLE: 1. The brother of one's father or mother; also applied to an aunt's husband; -- the correlative of aunt in sex, and of nephew and niece in relationship. 2. A pawnbroker. [Slang] Thackeray. URAEMIA: Accumulation in the blood of the principles of the urine, producing dangerous disease.
UNPLEADED: 1. Not used as a plea; not urged; as, an unpleaded excuse. 2. Not supported by pleas; undefended; as, an unpleaded suit.
UNBLOODY: Not bloody. Dryden. Unbloody sacrifice. (a) A sacrifice in which no victim is slain. (b) (R. C. Ch.) The Mass.
UNLOAD: 1. To take the load from; to discharge of a load or cargo; to disburden; as, to unload a ship; to unload a beast. 2. Hence, to relieve from anything onerous. 3. UNSOUL: To deprive of soul, spirit, or principle. [R.] Shelton.
UNKNOWN: Not known; not apprehended. -- Un*known"ness, n. [R.] Camden.
UNDULARY: Moving like waves; undulatory. [Obs.] Sir T. Browne.
UNDERDO: To do less than is requisite or proper; -- opposed to overdo. Grew. To do less thoroughly than is requisite; specifically, to cook insufficiently; as, to underdo the meat; -- opposed to overdo.
UNFASTEN: To loose; to unfix; to unbind; to untie.
UNVICAR: To deprive of the position or office a vicar. [R.] Strype.
UNLOCK: 1. To unfasten, as what is locked; as, to unlock a door or a chest. 2. To open, in general; to lay open; to undo. Unlock your springs, and open all your shades. Pope. [Lord] unlock the spell of sin. J. H. Newman.
UNPEOPLE: To deprive of inhabitants; to depopulate. Shak.
UPHILT: To thrust in up to the hilt; as, to uphilt one's sword into an enemy. [R.] Stanyhurst.
UNDEVIL: To free from possession by a devil or evil spirit; to exorcise. [Obs.] They boy having gotten a habit of counterfeiting . . . would not be undeviled by all their exorcisms. Fuller.
UNBE: To cause not to be; to cause to be another. [Obs. & R.] How oft, with danger of the field beset, Or with home mutinies, would he unbe Himself! Old Pay.
UNIQUITY: The quality or state of being unique; uniqueness. [R.] Walpole.
UNCONSTITUTIONAL: Not constitutional; not according to, or consistent with, the terms of a constitution of government; contrary to the constitution; as, an unconstitutional law, or act of an officer. Burke. -- Un*con`sti*tu"tion*al"i*ty, n. -- Un*con`sti*tu"tion*al-ly, adv.
UNDERSHAPEN: Under the usual shape or size; small; dwarfish. [Poetic] His dwarf, a vicious undershapen thing. Tennyson.
UPSTIR: Insurrection; commotion; disturbance. [Obs.] Sir J. Cheke.
UNTHREAD: 1. To draw or take out a thread from; as, to unthread a needle. 2. To deprive of ligaments; to loose the ligaments of. He with his bare wand can unthread thy joints. Milton. 3. To make one's way through; to traverse; as, to unthread a devious path. De Quincey.
UNWELLNESS: , n. Quality or state of being unwell.
ULMIN: A brown amorphous substance found in decaying vegetation. Cf. Humin. [Formerly written ulmine.]
UNCHRISTIANNESS: The quality or state of being unchristian. [R.] Eikon Basilike.
UNLEARN: 1. To forget, as what has been learned; to lose from memory; also, to learn the contrary of. I had learned nothing right; I had to unlearn everything. Milner. 2. To fail to learn. [Obs.] Dr. H. More.
UNAWARE: Not aware; not noticing; giving no heed; thoughtless; inattentive. Swift. Unawares. [Poetic] Dryden.
UBIETY: The quality or state of being in a place; local relation; position or location; whereness. [R.] Glanvill.
UNTIME: An unseasonable time. [Obs.] A man shall not eat in untime. Chaucer.
USUFRUCTUARY: A person who has the use of property and reaps the profits of it. Wharton. Of or pertaining to a usufruct; having the nature of a usufruct. The ordinary graces bequeathed by Christ to his church, as the usufructuary property of all its members. Coleridge.
UNALLOYED: Not alloyed; not reduced by foreign admixture; unmixed; unqualified; pure; as, unalloyed metals; unalloyed happiness. I enjoyed unalloyed satisfaction in his company. Mitford.
UNBIAS: To free from bias or prejudice. Swift.
UNWILLED: Deprived of the faculty of will or volition. Mrs. Browning.
UNITARIANIZE: To change or turn to Unitarian views.
UNDEAF: To free from deafness; to cause to hear. [Obs.] Shak.
UNBLINDFOLD: To free from that which blindfolds. Spenser.
UNCANONIZE: 1. To deprive of canonical authority. 2. To reduce from the rank of a canonized saint.
UNBREECH: 1. To remove the breeches of; to divest or strip of breeches. Shak. 2. (Gun.) To free the breech of, as a cannon, from its fastenings or coverings. Pennant.
UNCONCERN: Want of concern; absence of anxiety; freedom from solicitude; indifference. A listless unconcern, Cold, and averting from our neighbor's good. Thomson.
UNSCIENCE: Want of science or knowledge; ignorance. [Obs.] If that any wight ween a thing to be otherwise than it is, it is not only unscience, but it is deceivable opinion. Chaucer.
UNANSWERED: 1. Not answered; not replied; as, an unanswered letter. 2. Not refuted; as, an unanswered argument. 3. Not responded to in kind; unrequited; as, unanswered affection.
URANOLOGY: A discourse or treatise on the heavens and the heavenly bodies; the study of the heavens; uranography.
UPTHROW: To throw up. Drayton. See Throw, n., 9.
UMBRACULIFORM: Having the form of anything that serves to shade, as a tree top, an umbrella, and the like; specifically (Bot.), having the form of an umbrella; umbrella-shaped.
UNWISH: To wish not to be; to destroy by wishing. [Obs.] Now thou hast unwished five thousand men. Shak.
UPBRAID: 1. To charge with something wrong or disgraceful; to reproach; to cast something in the teeth of; -- followed by with or for, and formerly of, before the thing imputed. UNDERWOOD: Small trees and bushes that grow among large trees; coppice; underbrush; -- formerly used in the plural. Shrubs and underwoods look well enough while they grow within the shade of oaks and cedars. Addison.
UNSPAR: To take the spars, stakes, or bars from. [R.] Sir W. Scott.
UNDERGET: To get under or beneath; also, to understand. [Obs.] R. of Gloucester.
UNLESS: Upon any less condition than (the fact or thing stated in the sentence or clause which follows); if not; supposing that not; if it be not; were it not that; except; as, we shall fail unless we are industrious. UNSOCIABLE: Not sociable; not inclined to society; averse to companionship or conversation; solitary; reserved; as, an unsociable person or temper. -- Un*so"cia*ble*ness, n. -- Un*so"cia*bly, adv.
UNFRAME: To take apart, or destroy the frame of. Dryden.
UNSAFETY: The quality or state of being in peril; absence of safety; insecurity. Bacon.
UNREASONABLE: Not reasonable; irrational; immoderate; exorbitant. -- Un*rea"son*a*ble*ness, n. -- Un*rea"son*a*bly, adv.
UNSPECIALIZED: Not specialized; specifically (Biol.), not adapted, or set apart, for any particular purpose or function; as, an unspecialized unicellular organism. W. K. Brooks.
UNDERCLIFF: A subordinate cliff on a shore, consisting of material that has fallen from the higher cliff above.
UPHOLSTER: To furnish (rooms, carriages, bedsteads, chairs, etc.) with hangings, coverings, cushions, etc.; to adorn with furnishings in cloth, velvet, silk, etc.; as, to upholster a couch; to upholster a room with curtains. 1. A broker. [Obs.] Caxton. 2. An upholsterer. [Obs.] Strype.
UNDERSTANDINGLY: In an understanding manner; intelligibly; with full knowledge or comprehension; intelligently; as, to vote upon a question understandingly; to act or judge understandingly. The gospel may be neglected, but in can not be understandingly disbelieved. J. Hawes.
UNPOISED: 1. Not poised or balanced. 2. Not poised or weighed; hence, regardless of consequences; unhesitating. [Obs.] Marston.
UNISEXUAL: Having one sex only, as plants which have the male and female flowers on separate individuals, or animals in which the sexes are in separate individuals; dioecious; -- distinguished from bisexual, or hermaphrodite. See Dioecious.
UNWAYED: 1. Not used to travel; as, colts that are unwayed. [Obs.] Suckling. 2. Having no ways or roads; pathless. [Obs.] Wyclif.
UMLAUT: The euphonic modification of a root vowel sound by the influence of a, u, or especially i, in the syllable which formerly followed. Note: It is peculiar to the Teutonic languages, and was common in Anglo-Saxon. UNTHINK: To recall or take back, as something thought. Shak.
UNFLINCHING: Not flinching or shrinking; unyielding. -- Un*flinch"ing*ly, adv.
UNDERSKIRT: A petticoat; the foundation skirt of a draped dress.
UNBANK: To remove a bank from; to open by, or as if by, the removal of a bank. H. Taylor.
UNKINDLY: 1. Not kindly; unkind; ungracious. 2. Unnatural; contrary to nature. [Obs.] "Unkindly crime." Spenser. 3. Unfavorable; annoying; malignant. Milton.
UNIDEAL: 1. Not ideal; real; unimaginative. 2. Unideaed. [R.] Johnson.
URE: The urus. Use; practice; exercise. [Obs.] Fuller. Let us be sure of this, to put the best in ure That lies in us. Chapman. To use; to exercise; to inure; to accustom by practice. [Obs.] The French soldiers . . . from their youth have been practiced and ured in feats of arms. Sir T. More.
UNBURROW: To force from a burrow; to unearth.
UNIVERSAL: 1. Of or pertaining to the universe; extending to, including, or affecting, the whole number, quantity, or space; unlimited; general; all-reaching; all-pervading; as, universal ruin; universal good; universal benevolence or benefice. UNDEEDED: 1. Not deeded or transferred by deed; as, undeeded land. 2. Not made famous by any great action. [Obs.] Shak.
UNORIGINATED: 1. Not originated; existing from all eternity. F. W. Newman. 2. Not yet caused to be, or to be made; as, possible inventions still unoriginated.
ULCEROUS: 1. Having the nature or character of an ulcer; discharging purulent or other matter. R. Browning. 2. Affected with an ulcer or ulcers; ulcerated. It will but skin and film the ulcerous place. Shak. -- Ul"cer*ous*ly, adv. -- Ul"cer*ous*ness, n.
UNFALCATED: 1. Not falcated, or hooked. 2. Having no deductions; not curtailed, or shortened; undiminished. [R.] Swift.
UNIFORM: 1. Having always the same form, manner, or degree; not varying or variable; unchanging; consistent; equable; homogenous; as, the dress of the Asiatics has been uniform from early ages; the temperature is uniform; a stratum of uniform clay. UNEXTRICABLE: Not extricable; inextricable. [Obs.] Dr. H. More.
UPHEAPED: Piled up; accumulated. God, which shall repay all with upheaped measure. Udall.
ULTRAGASEOUS: Having the properties exhibited by gases under very low pressures (one millionth of an atmosphere or less). Matter under this condition, which has been termed the fourth state of matter, is sometimes called radiant matter.
UNIFLOROUS: Bearing one flower only; as, a uniflorous peduncle.
UNPROPER: Not proper or peculiar; improper. [Obs.] -- Un*prop"er*ly, adv. [Obs.]

A vessel of various forms, usually a vase furnished with a foot or pedestal, employed for different purposes, as for holding liquids, for ornamental uses, for preserving the ashes of the dead after cremation, and anciently for holding lots to be drawn. URANOMETRY: A chart or catalogue of fixed stars, especially of stars visible to the naked eye.
UNPROVIDE: To deprive of necessary provision; to unfurnish. Lest her . . . beauty unprovide my mind again. Shak.
UNHAND: To loose from the hand; to let go. Hold off! unhand me, gray beard loon! Eftsoons his hand dropped he. Coleridge.
UNSTOCK: 1. To deprive of a stock; to remove the stock from; to loose from that which fixes, or holds fast. 2. To remove from the stocks, as a ship.
URANYL: The radical UO2, conveniently regarded as a residue of many uranium compounds.
UNREGENERACY: The quality or state of being unregenerate. Glanvill.
UNWEIGHING: Not weighing or pondering; inconsiderate. Shak.
UMPIRAGE: 1. The office of an umpire; the power, right, or authority of an umpire to decide. The mind umpirage of the federal Union. E. Everett. 2. The act of umpiring; arbitrament. Bp. Hall.
UNDERYOKE: To subject to the yoke; to make subject. Wyclif.
UNLIKEN: To make unlike; to dissimilate. [Obs.] Wyclif.
UNDAUNTED: Not daunted; not subdued or depressed by fear. Shak. Syn. -- Bold; fearless; brave; courageous; intrepid. -- Un*daunt"ed*ly, adv. -- Un*daunt"ed*ness, n.
UNLOOSE: To make loose; to loosen; to set free. Shak. To become unfastened; to lose all connection or union.
UNBUCKLE: To loose the buckles of; to unfasten; as, to unbuckle a shoe. "Unbuckle anon thy purse." Chaucer.
UNDERSTUDY: To study, as another actor's part, in order to be his substitute in an emergency; to study another actor's part. One who studies another's part with a view to assuming it in an emergency.
UNTENANT: To remove a tenant from. [R.] Coleridge.
UNEDGE: To deprive of the edge; to blunt. J. Fletcher.
UNDERSLEEVE: A sleeve of an under-garment; a sleeve worn under another,
UNWONTED: 1. Not wonted; unaccustomed; unused; not made familiar by practice; as, a child unwonted to strangers. Milton. 2. Uncommon; unusual; infrequent; rare; as, unwonted changes. "Unwonted lights." Byron. -- Un*wont"ed*ly, adv. -- Un*wont"ed*ness, n.
UNLIKELINESS: The quality or state of being unlikely.
UNDERSIDE: The lower or lowest side of anything. Paley.
URCEOLATE: Shaped like a pitcher or urn; swelling below, and contrasted at the orifice, as a calyx or corolla.
UNGULATA: An extensive group of mammals including all those that have hoofs. It comprises the Artiodactyla and Perissodactyla.
UNCLOSED: 1. Not separated by inclosures; open. Clarendon. 2. Not finished; not concluded. [R.] Madison. 3. Not closed; not sealed; open. Byron.
UNDERDEALING: Crafty, unfair, or underhand dealing; unfair practice; trickery. Milton.
UNLEASH: To free from a leash, or as from a leash; to let go; to release; as, to unleash dogs.
UNEATH: Not easy; difficult; hard. [Obs.] Who he was, uneath was to descry. Spenser. Not easily; hardly; scarcely. [Obs.] Uneath may she endure the flinty streets. Shak.
UNSEEL: To open, as the eyes of a hawk that have been seeled; hence, to give light to; to enlighten. [Obs.] B. Jonson.
UPSHOOT: To shoot upward. "Trees upshooting high." Spenser.
UNSUIT: Not to suit; to be unfit for. [Obs.] Quarles.
ULARBURONG: A large East Indian nocturnal tree snake (Dipsas dendrophila). It is not venomous.
UNCONCERNED: Not concerned; not anxious or solicitous; easy in mind; carelessly secure; indifferent; as, to be unconcerned at what has happened; to be unconcerned about the future. -- Un`con*cern"ed*ly, adv. -- Un`con*cern"ed*ness, n. Happy mortals, unconcerned for more. Dryden.
UNIFORMITARIAN: Of, pertaining to, or designating, the view or doctrine that existing causes, acting in the same manner and with essentially the same intensity as at the present time, are sufficient to account for all geological changes. One who accepts uniformitarianism, or the uniformitarian doctrine.
URINOSE: Of or pertaining to urine, or partaking of its qualities; having the character or odor of urine; similar to urine. Arbuthnot.
UNDERSIZED: Of a size less than is common.
UPSET: 1. To set up; to put upright. [Obs.] "With sail on mast upset." R. of Brunne. 2. (a) To thicken and shorten, as a heated piece of iron, by hammering on the end. UDALMAN: Vars. of Odal, etc. Obs. exc. in Shetland and the Orkney Islands, where udal designates land held in fee simple without any charter and free of any feudal character. In the Shetland and Orkney Islands, one who holds property by udal, or allodial, right. Sir W. Scott.
UROHAEMATIN: Urinary hæmatin; -- applied to the normal coloring matter of the urine, on the supposition that it is formed either directly or indirectly (through bilirubin) from the hæmatin of the blood. See Urochrome, and Urobilin.
UNGELD: A person so far out of the protection of the law, that if he were murdered, no geld, or fine, should be paid, or composition made by him that killed him. Cowell. Burrill.
UNBLESS: To deprive of blessings; to make wretched. [Obs.] Shak.
UNDECKED: 1. Not decked; unadorned. [Eve] undecked, save with herself, more lovely fair. Milton. 2. Not having a deck; as, an undecked vessel.
UNWEMMED: Not blemished; undefiled; pure. [Obs.] Wyclif. With body clean and with unwemmed thought. Chaucer.
UNBENUMB: To relieve of numbness; to restore sensation to.
UNRESISTED: 1. Not resisted; unopposed. Bentley. 2. Resistless; as, unresisted fate. [R.] Pope.
UNTRAVELED: 1. Not traveled; not trodden by passengers; as, an untraveled forest. 2. Having never visited foreign countries; not having gained knowledge or experience by travel; as, an untraveled Englishman. Addison.
UNMASK: To strip of a mask or disguise; to lay open; to expose. To put off a mask. Shak.
URTICACEOUS: Of or pertaining to a natural order (Urticaceæ) of plants, of which the nettle is the type. The order includes also the hop, the elm, the mulberry, the fig, and many other plants.
UROSTEON: A median ossification back of the lophosteon in the sternum of some birds.
URINOMETER: A small hydrometer for determining the specific gravity of urine.
UNGUARD: To deprive of a guard; to leave unprotected. [R.] Sterne.
UNPOWER: Want of power; weakness. [Obs.] Piers Plowman.
UNIVERSALNESS: The quality or state of being universal; universality.
UNSHEATHE: To deprive of a sheath; to draw from the sheath or scabbard, as a sword. To unsheathe the sword, to make war.
UNGRACEFUL: Not graceful; not marked with ease and dignity; deficient in beauty and elegance; inelegant; awkward; as, ungraceful manners; ungraceful speech. The other oak remaining a blackened and ungraceful trunk. Sir W. Scott. -- Un*grace"ful*ly, adv. -- Un*grace"ful*ness, n.
UNGUIS: 1. The nail, claw, talon, or hoof of a finger, toe, or other appendage. 2. (Zoöl.) One of the terminal hooks on the foot of an insect. 3. (Bot.) The slender base of a petal in some flowers; a claw; called also ungula.
USURIOUS: 1. Practicing usury; taking illegal or exorbitant interest for the use of money; as, a usurious person. 2. Partaking of usury; containing or involving usury; as, a usurious contract. -- U*su"ri*ous*ly, adv. -- U*su"ri*ous*ness, n.
UNATTACHED: 1. Not attached; not adhering; having no engagement; free. 2. (Mil.) Not assigned to any company or regiment. 3. (Law) Not taken or arrested. R. Junius.
URCEOLE: A vessel for water for washing the hands; also, one to hold wine or water.
UNSETTLEDNESS: The quality or state of being unsettled.
UNWILLING: Not willing; loath; disinclined; reluctant; as, an unwilling servant. And drop at last, but in unwilling ears, This saving counsel, "Keep your piece nine years." Pope. -- Un*will"ing*ly, adv. -- Un*will"ing*ness, n.
UNASSENTED: Not assented; -- said specif. of stocks or bonds the holders of which refuse to deposit them by way of assent to an agreement altering their status, as in a readjustment.
UNBONE: 1. To deprive of bones, as meat; to bone. 2. To twist about, as if boneless. [R.] Milton.
URVA: The crab-eating ichneumon (Herpestes urva), native of India. The fur is black, annulated with white at the tip of each hair, and a white streak extends from the mouth to the shoulder.
URITE: One of the segments of the abdomen or post-abdomen of arthropods.
UNDERGROWTH: That which grows under trees; specifically, shrubs or small trees growing among large trees. Milton.
UNWONT: Unwonted; unused; unaccustomed. [Archaic] Sir W. Scott.
